reason: The cited evidence shows that CrCoNi (a ternary with no Mn) has a negative SFE and undergoes fcc-to-hcp transformation, supporting a link between Mn absence, SFE, and deformation mode. However, the hypothesis extends this to a general claim that reducing constituent count or Mn content enhances local order and lattice distortion, which is not directly evidenced in the cited passages; the role of local chemical order and lattice distortion as primary mediators is assumed rather than demonstrated.
premises: Reducing constituent count or Mn content enhances local chemical order and lattice distortion in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys.
Enhanced local order and lattice distortion lower stacking fault energy (SFE).
Lower SFE promotes twinning and/or fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Twinning and transformation increase yield strength and alter strain hardening relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline.
CrCoNi exhibits superior strength due to twinning/transformation linked to its negative SFE and absence of Mn.
